articles.title: Steven Spielberg’s 115-minute Sci-fi Masterpiece Soars Back to the Top of the Streaming Charts
articles.summary: More than 40 years after becoming one of the biggest movies of its era, Steven Spielberg’s beloved sci-fi hit is surging again on streaming.
body: Steven Spielberg has spent more than five decades making the kinds of movies that become permanent fixtures of pop culture.

Jaws practically invented the modern summer blockbuster, Raiders of the Lost Ark gave audiences one of cinema’s greatest adventure heroes, and Jurassic Park made dinosaurs feel real enough to terrify an entire generation. He’s also behind prestige dramas like Schindler’s List and Saving Private Ryan, while more recent films like West Side Story and The Fabelmans showed he was still finding new ways into familiar genres.

This year, he returned to science fiction with the well-received Disclosure Day, once again tapping into his fascination with extraterrestrial life. Now, one of Spielberg’s earliest sci-fi hits from the 1980s is back near the top of the streaming charts, giving audiences another reason to revisit the filmmaker’s long-running fascination with visitors from beyond Earth.
E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial, Spielberg’s beloved 1982 sci-fi classic and one of the most enduring movies of his career, is once again drawing viewers after being added to Apple TV earlier this month.

articles.title: Taylor Sheridan Meets 'Breaking Bad' in FX's Near-Perfect 10-Part Detective Thriller Series
articles.summary: Perhaps the most essential thing about adapting a movie into a TV show is getting the balance right between the old and the new. You want the show to feel like the movie and capture what you loved about the characters, but you also want enough new stuff going on to make the series a worthwhile…
body: Over the five seasons of the Fargo TV series, one of the most interesting things to see is just how much the vibe of Fargo (the movie) is included in each season. I’d argue that the first season has a bit too much, as it adheres very closely to the film to the point where you may even confuse some of the events of the two. And Martin Freeman’s character from season 1 is unmistakably similar to William H. Macy’s character from the film.

Season 4 likely doesn’t have enough Fargo in it. The change in location from Minnesota to St. Louis meant mostly losing the Minnesota accent which is so key to the sound of the film. And making it a period piece and more of a straight crime story was different too, which is maybe why many don’t like it.

Seasons 3 and 5 have a similar “dosage” of the film’s sensibilities. In those two seasons, you still feel the influence of the film, but there are so many original ideas going on that you might forget about the movie altogether — if not for the Minnesota accents to remind you.

articles.title: What we've been playing - "We're in danger of making this a regular thing"
articles.summary: Hello and welcome back to our regular feature where we write a little about the games we've been playing. This week, Mat J gets philosophical on us; Connor plays Minesweeper for some reason; and Bertie rallies the wonderful Eurogamer readers for a second week of Big Walk wholesome hilarity.
body: Here's another question: do you remember what you were playing last week? You don't have to! The What We've Been Playing archive has you covered.

If you don't spend a lot of time on Bluesky, a conversation about games that play themselves might have slipped the corners of your vision. If you'd like to read the inciting observation then head over to Jank. The argument's compelling enough: how much are we actually playing a video game that largely plays itself? What are we getting out of the experience if we don't really need to be that involved?

Critic Chris Franklin would point out this is a type of deconstruction which only really used to be levied at narrative games, that the absence of meaningful player interaction was in knowing the experience could only end along a predetermined path. It's new to extend that line of thinking to something like Vampire Survivors, where the goal is to reposition yourself for 30 minutes and essentially just select items you think will allow that to continue.

articles.title: Nintendo Blurred the Lines Between Handhelds and Consoles Decades Before the Switch
articles.summary: When the Super Nintendo officially launched in North America on Aug. 23, 1991, Nintendo immediately set to work proving the hardware could offer ambitious experiences the original NES simply could not.
body: For a long time after its release, the Super Nintendo played host to some of the most visually stimulating games of its era. Then came the Super FX chip and the prerendered visuals of Donkey Kong Country and its sequels. But there was still room for experiences that didn’t rely on cutting-edge visuals and new franchises, or indeed, anything new at all.

Introduced in mid-1994, the Super Game Boy was an oversized cartridge with a slot that turned the Super Nintendo into another device to play your library of Game Boy and supported Game Boy Color games (clear cartridges exclusive to the newer handheld simply displayed error screens). It accomplished this feat not through emulation, but by including a CPU like the ones inside an actual Game Boy. The approach wasn’t quite perfect, as the clock speed differed slightly, but it came reasonably close.

articles.title: The Sinking City 2 Review
articles.summary: The Sinking City 2 feels inescapably like off-brand Resident Evil, but it's a praiseworthy imitation of its main inspirations wrapped in the Cthulhu mythos.
body: It was impossible for me to play The Sinking City 2 for more than 15 minutes without coming to the obvious realization that this is Resident Evil in a fedora. That might sound dismissive, but I really enjoy the recent Resident Evil games, so comparing Frogwares' Lovecraftian survival horror sequel to some of the best of them – which feels especially similar to 2019's Resident Evil 2 remake – is much more of a compliment than a put-down. What sets it apart begins with its unique, rich, 1920s New England setting flush with loving detail that instills a strong sense of personality over the top of the mechanics it so clearly imitates.

You play as Calvin Rafferty, a likeable occultist waking up to an apocalyptic flood set to wipe out the entire city of Arkham, Massachusetts in 1929. He's definitely a little bit of a pulp fiction stock character: hard-chinned, two-fisted, and foolishly brave. But there are layers to him that rise to the surface here and there. Similar to the Resident Evil comparison, likening him to the classic heroes of the genre is not really an insult.

articles.title: 'Hoping for a Huge October Surprise, But Not Holding My Breath' — Arc Raiders Players Torn After Embark Delays Future Expeditions Until Early 2027
articles.summary: Embark Studios has announced that all future Arc Raiders Expeditions have been delayed until early 2027 as it aims to "return with major improvements" following community feedback.
body: The developer behind the early 2026 extraction shooter hit announced the change in its post-launch schedule in an update on the Arc Raiders website today. It came with confirmation that Expedition 5 will launch when the window opens September 8 and close September 29, but after that, the Rust Belt will be quieter than normal.

"We have been carefully reviewing your feedback on Expeditions," Embark's post said, "and while we've made ongoing improvements along the way, we've come to realize that some of the issues you've raised, like the tight departure windows, the reward structure, and accessibility for new players, need more than incremental fixes. They call for bigger changes."

"In order to address those concerns, we need to pause the Expeditions for a while. The fifth Expedition will be the last one until early 2027, when Expeditions will return with major improvements, tackling some of the biggest player pain points. So, if you’ve been on the fence about departing - now is the time! We will share more details on what those changes will look like in September."
points: Embark Studios has announced that all future Arc Raiders Expeditions have been delayed until early 2027 as it aims to "return with major improvements" following community feedback.

articles.title: 5 Times Disney’s Sci-Fi Ambitions Crashed and Burned at the Box Office
articles.summary: Disney has never shied away from high-stakes science fiction. By rendering Pixar’s digital landscapes and mapping Marvel ’s cosmic universe, the studio has spent decades proving audiences will follow it into the unknown.
body: These aren’t just mild disappointments; they're tentpole releases backed by huge budgets, A-list talent, and groundbreaking VFX. Some were pitched as the next Pirates of the Caribbean, while others were original concepts meant to spawn new franchises.

Yet even a headline-grabbing box office run can mask a total financial disaster once production and marketing costs enter the ledger. From dead-on-arrival franchise starters to high-concept animated flops, these are five of Disney’s biggest sci-fi box office catastrophes — and a brief look at how they went so spectacularly off the rails.

Dedicated entirely to Buzz Lightyear, one of the most recognizable characters in the Toy Story franchise, 2022's Lightyear had perhaps the safest concept on this list. Despite that, it inevitably became one of Pixar's rare theatrical disappointments. Directed by Angus MacLane, the film was pitched as the in-universe blockbuster that inspired the original Toy Story action figure. With Chris Evans replacing Tim Allen as the voice of Buzz, Pixar used the spinoff to trade its usual toy-centric antics for a surprisingly conventional sci-fi adventure.

articles.title: Double Fine Owns IP and Publishing Rights for All of Its Games Following Xbox Split, Psychonauts Studio Confirms
articles.summary: Psychonauts and Brutal Legend developer Double Fine Productions has confirmed it has regained the IP and publishing rights for all of its games released under Microsoft following its split from Xbox.
body: CEO Tim Schafer cleared the air about the developer's future in the industry during a conversation with Kinda Funny Games today. Amid questions from fans hoping to support Double Fine as it enters a new chapter, he clarified that buying any of its previous releases will help it continue to flex the wildly creative muscles it's known for.
"I saw a question, there, 'Do you guys make the money on games?' The transfer of the IP came back to us, and we get the publishing rights back to all our games," Schafer said.

The one caveat to all of this is that it may still say Microsoft owns "some of them," but that will change in time. He went on, explaining, "it just takes a while for it to all process." The headline, though, is that "when people buy our games, it supports the studio."
"If you're curious, buying any of our games helps support the studio," he repeated. "We can turn that money into revenue that helps us extend that runway."

articles.title: Call Of Duty’s Most Controversial Item Is Back In Modern Warfare 4, But With Some Major Changes
articles.summary: One of the most infamous and controversial items in Call of Duty is the Riot Shield. Some love it. Some hate it. Well, it's back in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, but with a few key changes. With MW4's beta now live, we're seeing the game in action and learning more about it.
body: "In use, the shield provides frontal protection while advancing or holding a position. It can also be used offensively, with a new heavy melee attack that knocks enemies down and creates space in close quarters," Activision said.

When planted in the ground, players can mount their weapons to it for improved stability. The Riot Shield can also be used strategically in MW4's objective-based modes where players hunker down in one particular spot.

To balance things out, Activision made the Riot Shield destructible in MW4. In the past, it could soak up bullets like a sponge, and people loved and hated that. In MW4, it's "durable enough to support a push or cover a retreat." However, it will eventually break, and Activision said that should encourage players to use it strategically as opposed to opting for "sustained use."

The MW4 beta is going on now for people who preordered the game. An open beta, meanwhile, runs August 28-September 1, and that doesn't require any preorder. The beta includes not just multiplayer, but also a campaign mission, Entrenched, and a glimpse at the future of Call of Duty: Warzone.

articles.title: GTA 6 Leaker Has Not Been Identified Yet – Report
articles.summary: One of the biggest stories in gaming this week has been the ongoing GTA 6 gameplay leaks, which are all about hyping up a memecoin for profit. A new report provides insight into how Rockstar is handling the situation internally.
body: Bloomberg reported that Rockstar has yet to identify the party responsible, or how such a breach happened. One top executive at Rockstar sent a memo to staff this week "denouncing the leaker and promising the incident wouldn't detract from the excellent work they've done," the report said.

Additionally, it was reported that Rockstar is not planning to change its marketing plans for GTA 6 due to the leak. Some had theorized that the leak might have some effect on the planned reveal on Netflix on August 27, but that's apparently not going to be the case.
After GTA 6's first trailer leaked in December 2023, Rockstar responded in real time and released the trailer ahead of schedule, so there is precedent to Rockstar altering plans based on leaks.

GTA 6 suffered a massive leak in 2022. At the time, Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick said it was “really frustrating and upsetting,” but the leaks had no financial impact on the company. Take-Two lost more than $2 billion in its total value this week since the latest leaks began, but there could be any number of different reasons for that apart from the leaks.

articles.title: Rockstar employees frustrated by GTA 6 leaks, though they may have only whet appetites for the reveal
articles.summary: Bloomberg's Jason Schreier reports that some Rockstar employees are feeling "angry" and "frustrated" that, despite submitting to strict security measures following the 2022 hack that revealed Grand Theft Auto 6 to the world—namely the abolishment of remote work—a leak has once again sprung.
body: Someone going by the name "Cyberleek" has been posting new GTA 6 gameplay clips every day for the past few days. The leaker may even have access to a build of GTA 6, though it's unclear if it's the full game or only a portion.
Meanwhile, the official GTA 6 reveal is still scheduled for next week, and will still air exclusively on Netflix for the first six hours.

It's unlikely that the leaks will have any measurable impact on GTA 6's sales. It's already sold an "unprecedented" number of preorders, according to Take-Two. I doubt the Netflix reveal will be harmed, either: The circulating gameplay clips make it slightly less of an event, but the leaker's low-quality, watermarked videos have only whet my appetite for the proper reveal.
It's easy to find similar sentiments around the internet: "I was a little hyped for GTA 6 but after the leaks I'm even more hyped than ever and can't wait for the extended look," says one poster.

articles.title: CoD: MW4 DLC Honors Real-Life Medal Of Honor Recipient Who Lost His Eye And Teeth In Grenade Blast
articles.summary: Activision has announced that Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 will have day-one DLC, and like in years past, it will focus on a real-life military hero, with proceeds going to charity.
body: The Call of Duty Endowment Valor Pack, launching on October 23 alongside the game, adds the real-life Medal of Honor recipient Kyle Carpenter to the game as a playable character.

Carpenter was in Marjah, Afghanistan, when, on November 21, 2010, he put himself in front of a grenade to help save the life of his fellow Marine, Nick Eufrazio. Carpenter sustained serious injuries from the grenade blast. He was unconscious for five weeks, had his teeth stripped from his mouth, and lost an eye. He sustained numerous other life-threatening injuries in the blast.
Carpenter received the Medal of Honor from President Barack Obama in 2014. "No matter how wrecked your world gets, the world keeps spinning," Carpenter said in the video below.

The Call of Duty Endowment is Activision's charity that supports military veterans and specifically helping soldiers find jobs after leaving the service. Proceeds from this new Valor Pack will benefit the endowment.

articles.title: Mortal Shell 2’s Latest Update Alleviates One Of The Game’s Biggest Headaches
articles.summary: Developer Cold Symmetry has released its latest souls-like action-RPG, Mortal Shell 2, on August 20 for PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S. And not even a day after launch, the studio already dropped a patch that makes some welcome tweaks, including addressing one of the game's most annoying…
body: On August 20, Cold Symmetry shared a breakdown on the game's subreddit and Steam page of what Balance Patch 1 does.

A welcome adjustment is a refund of the Glimpses--a rare currency used to bond with and unlock memories of your shell--you might've spent to discover a shell's location. You get whatever you spent back, and now, instead of costing that rare currency, buying a shell map costs Gloom, this game's version of Runes or Souls.

A big change is a nerf to a handful of bosses and enemies. As Cold Symmetry put it, "all enemies featured in the beta were restored to their beta HP values." This means that the starting area of Mortal Shell 2 has been tuned down to match what was in the beta, which I found quite easy when compared to the full release.

Maybe the most major tweak, however, is an increase to the amount of gold you find now. As a result of this patch, gold drops from enemies have been "significantly increased," especially in the second zone. This lets you upgrade your weapons more often, as gold discovery should be in line with the materials you find everywhere.
